Core Active Vocabulary (5 items):

shirt — a garment for the upper body. Example: I am wearing a white shirt.
trousers — a garment for the legs. Example: These trousers are new.
jeans — trousers made of denim. Example: I am wearing blue jeans.
dress — a woman's one-piece garment. Example: My sister is wearing a dress.
skirt — a garment worn by women below the waist. Example: She is wearing a red skirt.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• I am wearing ...
• These jeans are new.
• That dress is nice.
• What are you wearing?
• Those trousers are blue.

TROU-sers, JEANS
Listen and repeat three times.
Which word carries the main stress?
Grammar focus: Demonstratives (this/that/these/those).
Use this and these for things near you, that and those for things further away: this shirt, these jeans, that dress, those trousers. Trousers and jeans are always plural.

Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
Today I am wearing a white shirt and blue jeans. My sister is wearing a dress and my mother is wearing a skirt. These trousers are new.
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.
A: What are you wearing today? B: A shirt and jeans. A: Are those trousers new? B: Yes, they are.
